messages:
claire: Quick poll: if you could play exactly one board game for the rest of your life (no expansions), which would it be and why? :thinking_face:

mike: Catan. Keeps changing every game, so it never gets stale. :boat:

sophia: Hive. Compact, abstract, perfect 2-player brainburners. No need for setup space. :beetle:

alex: Ticket to Ride. Chill, social, and I like maps. Also easy to teach to guests.

maria: Chess. Classic, infinite depth. Also I like the elegance of rules. :chess_pawn:

devin: Pandemic. Cooperative! I prefer teamwork over cutthroat conquest.

kitchen-bot: Poll created: Catan, Hive, Ticket to Ride, Chess, Pandemic — vote with :thumbsup:, :heart:, :tada:, :eyes:, :raised_hands:

mike: voted :thumbsup:

sophia: voted :heart:

alex: voted :tada:

maria: voted :eyes:

devin: voted :raised_hands:

claire: Noticing a theme: strategy over party games. Any underrated picks?

ashley: Azul. Pretty satisfying pattern play, and those tiles tho. :blue_square:

devin: Gloomhaven? Too much reading perhaps but the campaign > everything.

sophia: Love Azul but solo variants can be meh. Hive scales best 2-player imo.

claire: Thanks all! Small follow-up: any one-line recommendation for a new player to each game?

mike: Catan: trade early, build roads to new spots.

alex: Ticket to Ride: block when someone is close to completing a long route.

maria: Chess: control center, don't lose your bishops for pawns.

devin: Pandemic: share info, plan moves ahead.

sophia: Hive: think one step deeper than your opponent.

claire: Saved — maybe team game night next Friday? :calendar:

devin: I'm in.

ashley: count me in!
